title: Promise, prediction, description, and commendation
summary: A promise communicates a commitment to bring about a result or take an action. A prediction communicates an expectation about what is likely to happen.
notes:
The distinction depends on the words and the circumstances in which they were used. In Hawkins, the doctor’s specific guarantee and repeated solicitation of the operation could support a finding of commitment, while estimates of the recovery period remained predictions. In Bayliner, the performance figures described a differently equipped boat, and the advertising praise did not promise a particular speed. Ask what a reasonable recipient could understand the speaker to have undertaken, and identify the evidence supporting that understanding.

Hawkins distinguishes an asserted guarantee from estimates of recovery time. Bayliner distinguishes a performance description of another configuration and general promotional praise from a warranty about the goods sold. A statement’s specificity, its relation to the actual subject, and its place in the transaction matter. A disappointing outcome alone does not establish a promise. The textbook’s theories of promise then ask why a sufficiently identified assurance should receive legal enforcement.
